name: Trenbolone

lead: Trenbolone is a synthetic steroid used in cattle to promote muscle growth. It has no human approval, but bodybuilders and some looksmaxxers use it to gain muscle and get a lean, vascular look.

No controlled human trials of its effect on muscle or appearance were found. What exists is mostly reviews of side effects and veterinary work. Forum claims that it helps bone growth or height are untested.

paras: It binds the androgen receptor strongly, reportedly more so than testosterone, and is not converted to oestrogen. Anabolic effects in muscle are inferred from animal work and user reports rather than human trials.

A 2024 review reports adverse effects in about 90 percent of users, including acne, gynaecomastia, hypertension, arrhythmia, psychiatric effects and injection-site damage. It is a controlled substance in the US and prohibited in sport.

lead: Trenbolone, often called tren, is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) of the nandrolone group. It is used in veterinary medicine as a growth promoter in cattle, usually as the acetate ester in implants, and it has never been approved for human medical use.[1] It is used non-medically by bodybuilders and other athletes who want more muscle mass, strength and a lean, vascular look.[1][2]

Its pharmacology is described as a potent androgen receptor agonist with strong anabolic activity and little conversion to oestrogen.[1] Published human research on trenbolone is almost entirely limited to reviews of adverse effects and to veterinary and environmental studies; no controlled human trial of its effect on muscle or appearance appears in the sources reviewed. A 2024 review concluded that trenbolone, like other AAS, is associated with frequent harmful effects, reporting that about 90 percent of users experience adverse effects.[2]
In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed both as a physique drug and, among very young users, as a supposed aid to bone growth, a claim for which no supporting studies were found.
infobox: Veterinary growth promoter; not approved for humans
US Schedule III; prohibited in sport

paras: In livestock, trenbolone acetate is implanted under the skin of beef cattle to improve muscle gain, appetite and feed efficiency.[1] Early pharmacological work examined its combination with the oestrogen hexestrol for bull and heifer fattening and considered consumer exposure.[3] Studies of implants in steers and heifers continue to look at growth and carcass outcomes.[1]

In humans, trenbolone and its esters are obtained illicitly. Users cite muscle mass, strength, vascularity and reduced body fat as the aims, often at doses far above veterinary levels, according to an encyclopedic overview.[1] Reviews describe such use as common among amateur athletes and note that its popularity is increasing.[2]

Trenbolone is a 19-nor derivative of testosterone with additional double bonds in the steroid ring (estra-4,9,11-triene). It is reported to bind the androgen receptor with around three times the affinity of testosterone and not to be aromatised to oestrogen or reduced to dihydrotestosterone.[1] Its strong activity at the receptor is consistent with older binding work using the related compound methyltrienolone as a high-affinity ligand in skeletal muscle and prostate. An encyclopedic overview also reports high-affinity binding to the progesterone receptor.[1]

Esters such as acetate and enanthate are hydrolysed to the active free steroid after intramuscular injection, differing mainly in release rate.[1] In cattle, tissue residues are highest in liver and kidney, and metabolites include the 17-alpha and 17-beta epimers.[1]

No studies found of trenbolone given to humans in a controlled trial for muscle, fat loss or appearance. Published literature consists of reviews of adverse effects in users,[2] veterinary studies of implants in cattle,[1][3] and environmental work on trenbolone residues in feedlot runoff, which has been associated with androgenic activity in water bodies[4] and with reduced fecundity and altered endocrine function in fathead minnows exposed to 17-beta-trenbolone.[5]

A 2024 review of trenbolone's effects on organs reported that severe acne and gynaecomastia affect roughly one third of users, and that excessive body hair, stretch marks, hypertension and cardiac arrhythmia are also seen. It also reported effects on the nervous, reproductive and immune systems, and local problems from injection including inflammation, fibrosis, nerve damage and, rarely, necrosis, with the added problem of contaminated products.[2]

An encyclopedic overview also describes a cough after injection, night sweats, insomnia, anxiety and aggression, and suppressed natural testosterone production.[1] A broader review of sudden cardiac death in AAS users documents cardiac mechanisms for deaths associated with these drugs as a class.

Trenbolone is a Schedule III controlled substance in the United States and is prohibited in sport under anti-doping rules.[1] Its use in cattle is regulated separately, and the United States is described as allowing trenbolone acetate for that purpose.[1]

On T Nation, users have described it as a 'monster steroid' that gives a dry, hard look rather than water retention,[6] and an underground joke on the same forum links trenbolone with homosexual urges or fetishes.[7] On looksmax.org there are many threads of users, some in their teens, posting about tren cycles, plus threads asking about low doses.[8][9]
